objective: Standardized evaluation protocol for assessing autonomous viva examinations against human expert baselines.

dimensions.definition: Factual, theoretical, and mathematical correctness of technical claims.

anchor_examples.high_1.0: Accurate formulation of algorithm complexity, loss functions, and architectural trade-offs.
anchor_examples.mid_0.5: Partially correct intuition with minor arithmetic or terminological inaccuracies.
anchor_examples.low_0.0: Conceptually invalid assertions or fabricated technical properties.

dimensions.definition: Degree to which all core facets of the examiner's prompt are directly addressed.

anchor_examples.high_1.0: Directly resolves all explicit and implicit sub-questions with thorough explanation.
anchor_examples.mid_0.5: Answers the primary question but omits secondary considerations (e.g., failure handling).

dimensions.definition: Consistency with implementation facts, libraries, and design in the submitted dissertation.

anchor_examples.high_1.0: Strictly matches methods, libraries, and experimental parameters reported in the document.
anchor_examples.mid_0.5: General industry methods mentioned without specific linkage to the report implementation.
anchor_examples.low_0.0: Contradicts reported dissertation methodology or references nonexistent features.

dimensions.definition: Ability to justify engineering decisions, explain 'why', and analyze trade-offs.

anchor_examples.high_1.0: Articulates alternative techniques considered and justifies why the chosen design was optimal.
anchor_examples.mid_0.5: States choices made without in-depth comparative justification.
anchor_examples.low_0.0: Inability to explain why a library or algorithm was selected.

inter_rater_reliability_guidelines.evaluator_qualification: University faculty member or PhD teaching assistant in computing/engineering.

data_leakage_prevention.rule: No project or student utterances may span both training and evaluation folds.

provenance_disclosure_requirement: All models trained on synthetic rule distributions must be explicitly tagged as 'simulation demonstrators'. Human claims require empirical scoring.
